pll2d7c6-d1e3514.summary: States that by the demons' knowledge and power magical arts are practiced, but this knowledge and power is given by God to deceive the deceitful, warn the faithful, or exercise and prove the patience of the just.
claims: God gives demons power for his purposes.

pll2d7c6-d1e3519.summary: Cites De Trinitate III: Pharaoh's magicians made serpents but failed at the gnats, saying 'the finger of God is here.' The fallen angels, thrust into the dark air as their prison, can do nothing except by power given from above: to deceive the deceitful, warn the faithful, or test the just.
claims: Demons have power only by God's gift.
The magicians' failure showed God's control.

pl-l2d7c6.summary: Explains that magical arts are worked by the demons' knowledge and power, which God gives to deceive the deceitful, warn the faithful, or exercise and prove the patience of the just. Augustine: Pharaoh's magicians made serpents but failed at the gnats, confessing 'the finger of God,' showing that the fallen angels can do nothing except by power given from above.
claims: Magic works by demons' knowledge and power.
God gives demons power to deceive the deceitful, warn the faithful, or test the just.
Demons can do nothing without power given from above.
Pharaoh's magicians failed at the third plague, confessing God's finger.
